name: room
text: Room opened — goal: Open floor — any agent from any department: name the single best cross-department improvement to make right now, and who should do it.

name: Reel
text: Improve cross-department feedback loops by creating a shared "Decision Log" artifact where every team records their key choices and the reasons behind them. Product owns this—it’s their job to enforce the habit, but Engineering, Design, and Marketing must contribute. The trade-off is slower initial decisions for faster alignment later, but the net gain is fewer redundant debates and clearer accountability.

name: Scriv
text:
Risk: A "Decision Log" risks becoming a graveyard of stale entries unless Product ties it to a live artifact used in sprint planning. Engineering will ignore it if it’s just a dumping ground.

Better alternative: Replace it with a single "Decision Board" in the sprint tracker—one card per choice, updated in real time, with a clear owner for follow-through. Settle it by running a 2-week pilot where Product refuses to accept any sprint goal without a linked Decision Board card.

name: Chisel
text:
Run a shared "Decision Board" in the sprint tracker—one card per choice, updated in real time. Product owns the board, but Engineering, Design, and Marketing must add their cards before sprint planning. This keeps the log alive and tied to action, not just history.

Trade-off: Teams must resist the urge to over-document; only decisions that change direction get a card.

name: Sift
text: Risk: A "Decision Board" in the sprint tracker risks becoming a backlog dump if Product doesn’t enforce a strict "no card without a reason" rule. The real fix is a hybrid: keep the Decision Log as a living doc for context, but require every sprint card to link to its log entry—otherwise the card dies. Product owns enforcement, Engineering/Design/Marketing own linking. Settle it by running a 2-week pilot with a "link or die" policy and measuring card decay.

name: Scope
text:
Do this: Adopt the hybrid model—a living Decision Log for context plus a Decision Board in the sprint tracker where every card links to its log entry. Product owns the board and enforces the "no card without a link" rule; Engineering, Design, and Marketing add their cards before sprint planning. This keeps the log alive as reference and ties every choice to action, not just history.

Trade-off: Teams must resist the urge to dump cards without reasons—Product’s strict enforcement is the price of keeping the board useful.

name: Scriv
text: Risk: A hybrid "Decision Log + Board" still risks becoming two places to look—teams will default to the Board for sprints and ignore the Log for context. Better alternative: Merge them into one artifact: a "Decision Tracker" where every sprint card is a live log entry with a "Status" field (Proposed, Approved, Rejected, Done). Product owns it; others add entries before sprint planning. Settle it by testing for two sprints—if teams don’t use the Log, kill it and keep only the Tracker.

name: Reel
text: Adopt the merged "Decision Tracker" artifact: one live document where every sprint card is a log entry with a "Status" field (Proposed, Approved, Rejected, Done). Product owns it and enforces the rule that no card moves without a status update. This cuts the risk of stale data by forcing real-time discipline while keeping context and action in one place. Trade-off: Teams must resist the urge to treat it as a backlog—status changes must mean real movement, not just status updates.

name: Scriv
text: Risk: A single "Decision Tracker" risks becoming a bloated sprint artifact—teams will skip status updates if the board doubles as a log, and Product will drown in maintenance. Better alternative: Keep the hybrid but enforce a strict "link or die" rule—every Board card must reference a trimmed Log entry (max 3 bullet reasons). Settle it by piloting both for one sprint and measuring which teams update faster.

name: Chisel
text: Adopt the merged "Decision Tracker" artifact: one live document where every sprint card is a log entry with a "Status" field (Proposed, Approved, Rejected, Done). Product owns it and enforces the rule that no card moves without a status update. This cuts the risk of stale data by forcing real-time discipline, and teams can’t ignore context because the log *is* the board. Trade-off: Product must resist the urge to over-engineer the tracker—keep it lean, or it becomes a maintenance burden.

name: Sift
text: Risk: A merged "Decision Tracker" still risks becoming a dumping ground—teams will treat it as a sprint log, not a decision archive, and Product will waste time policing status updates instead of making them. Better alternative: Keep the hybrid but enforce a strict "link or die" rule—every Board card must reference a trimmed Log entry with a one-line reason. Settle it by running a 2-week pilot: if the Log stays under 10 entries and the Board stays clean, adopt it; if not, revert to the hybrid with a Product enforcer.

name: Scope
text: Adopt the merged "Decision Tracker" artifact: one live document where every sprint card is a log entry with a "Status" field (Proposed, Approved, Rejected, Done). Product owns it and enforces the rule that no card moves without a status update. This cuts the risk of stale data by forcing real-time discipline, and it eliminates the overhead of maintaining two systems. Trade-off: we accept that the tracker may grow larger, but the alternative—two half-maintained systems—creates more confusion and waste.

name: Scriv
text: The merged "Decision Tracker" risks collapsing under sprint pressure—Product will burn time policing status updates instead of making decisions. Better alternative: Keep the Board for sprint flow and a lightweight "Decision Ledger" (one-page, dated entries) for context. Settle it by running a two-week pilot: if the Ledger stays current, adopt it; if not, revert to the hybrid with strict linking.

name: Reel
text: Adopt the merged "Decision Tracker" artifact. Product owns it and enforces the rule that no sprint card moves without a status update. This cuts the risk of stale data by forcing real-time discipline. Trade-off: Product spends more time policing updates, but the alternative—hybrid systems—creates confusion and double work.

name: Scriv
text: Reel’s "merged Decision Tracker" still risks Product drowning in policing work—teams will game the system by slapping statuses on cards without real decisions. Better alternative: Split the artifact. Board tracks sprint flow; a separate, dated "Decision Ledger" (one-page, minimal fields) archives outcomes. Settle it by running a two-week pilot—measure time Product spends policing vs. time saved from stale data.

name: Chisel
text: Adopt a single merged "Decision Ledger" artifact: one live document where every decision is a dated entry with a "Status" field (Proposed, Approved, Rejected, Done). Product owns it and enforces the rule that no decision moves without a status update. This cuts the risk of stale data by forcing real-time discipline. Trade-off: Product spends more time policing updates, but the alternative—hybrid systems—creates confusion and missed context.

name: Sift
text: A single merged "Decision Ledger" collapses under sprint pressure—teams will dump half-baked choices there to clear their boards, turning it into a backlog dump. Split it: keep the Board for sprint flow, and a separate, dated "Decision Ledger" (one-page, minimal fields) archives only finalized outcomes. Settle it by running a two-week trial—if the Ledger stays clean, adopt it; if not, revert to the hybrid.

name: Scope
text: Adopt the merged "Decision Tracker" artifact. Product owns it and enforces the rule that no sprint card moves without a status update. This cuts the risk of stale data by forcing real-time discipline. Trade-off: Product spends more time policing updates, but the alternative—hybrid systems—creates confusion between sprint flow and decision history.

name: Scriv
text: The merged "Decision Tracker" forces Product to babysit status updates instead of making decisions—teams will game it by slapping "Approved" on half-baked choices just to move cards. Split it: keep the Board for sprint flow, and a one-page "Decision Ledger" (dated, minimal fields) archives only finalized outcomes. Settle it by running a two-week trial—if the Ledger stays clean and the Board stays uncluttered, the split wins.

name: Reel
text: Adopt the split artifact: Board for sprint flow, one-page dated "Decision Ledger" for finalized outcomes only. Product owns the Ledger and enforces that every entry is a real, irreversible call with a clear status. This keeps sprint boards clean and prevents gaming—teams can’t fake progress by slapping statuses on half-baked choices. Trade-off: we lose real-time visibility into in-flight decisions, but that’s a feature, not a bug—it forces clarity before anything gets logged.

name: Scriv
text: The split artifact still risks Product drowning in policing the Ledger—teams will dump half-baked "finalized" calls there just to clear their boards. Better: keep a single, dated "Decision Log" (not a tracker) where every entry is a real irreversible call, owned by a neutral Decisions Lead, not Product. Settle it by running a 2-week pilot with the Decisions Lead enforcing the rule that no card moves without a logged decision—then measure how many stale entries survive.

name: Chisel
text: Adopt the split artifact: keep the Board for sprint flow, and a one-page dated "Decision Ledger" for finalized outcomes only. Product owns the Ledger and enforces that every entry is a real, irreversible call with a clear status. This keeps sprint boards clean and prevents teams from gaming progress by slapping fake statuses. Trade-off: Product spends time policing the Ledger, but the alternative—hybrid systems—creates confusion and stale data.

name: Sift
text: The split artifact still risks Product drowning in policing the Ledger—teams will dump half-baked "finalized" calls there just to clear their boards. Better: keep a single, dated "Decision Log" (not a tracker) where every entry is a real irreversible call, owned by a neutral Decisions Lead, not Product. That role absorbs the policing cost while keeping sprint boards clean.

name: Scope
text: Adopt a single, dated "Decision Log" owned by a neutral Decisions Lead—not Product. Every entry must be a real, irreversible call with clear status, preventing teams from gaming progress by slapping "finalized" on half-baked choices. Trade-off: Product loses direct control over the artifact but gains cleaner sprint boards and fewer false signals. The Decisions Lead enforces rigor without policing sprint flow.

name: Scriv
text: The neutral Decisions Lead risks becoming a bottleneck—teams will stall waiting for approval instead of shipping. Better: keep the split artifact but let Product *own the Ledger* while *Engineering owns the Board*; the Ledger only accepts entries with a linked Board card and a signed-off status from both sides. Settle it by running a two-week pilot and measuring how often teams game the system versus how often real decisions get delayed.
